summary: Sarah J. Horton works in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. She studied at Yale University under Stanley Weinstein and served as an assistant professor at Macalester College (attested 2006).

Sarah Shaw is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at the University of Oxford under Richard Gombrich and Lance S. Cousins. In 2013, she held posts at Oxford's Faculty of Oriental Studies, Wolfson College, and OCBS.
Saraju Rath is an Indologist and linguist who held positions at the International Institute for Asian Studies, attested in 2012 and 2022.

Sarasi Kumar Saraswati (1906–1983) was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied under Sivaprasad Bhattacharyya and Jitendra Nath Banerjea, served as Librarian at The Asiatic Society, and held a post at the University of Calcutta.

Sarat Chandra Das (1849–1917) was an Indologist and Tibetologist who studied at Presidency University, Presidency College, Chennai, and the University of Calcutta. He was director of Bhutia Boarding School (1874) and Tibetan translator for Bengal (1881–1904).
Sarat Sarma is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies who earned a PhD at Manipur University (attested 2006), studying under S. Shyamkishore Singh and S. Lokendrajit Singh.
Saroja Bhate (b. 1942) is a scholar of Indology and linguistics who served as a professor at Savitribai Phule Pune University from around 1980 to 2002, and was attested there again in 2011.

Sarva Daman Singh is a scholar of Indology, history, and archaeology. He held posts at the University of Queensland, serving as Professor of History (attested 1958) and remaining affiliated there through at least 1987.

Sarvepalli Gopal (1923–2002) was a historian who studied at the University of Madras, Presidency College, Chennai, Madras Christian College, Mill Hill School, and Balliol College, Oxford (~1948–1951). He held a post at Jawaharlal Nehru University (~1971–1987).

Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan (1888–1975) was a philosopher and Indologist who studied at Voorhees College, Madras Christian College, and the University of Madras. He served as professor at Calcutta and Oxford, and as Vice-Chancellor at Andhra and Banaras Hindu universities.
Saswati Mutsuddy is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied under Dipak Kumar Barua and served as an assistant professor of Pali at the University of Calcutta (attested 2011).

Satiranjan Sen worked in Sinology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Peking University, founded Cheen Bharat Sanskriti, and served as a research scholar and junior research fellow at Visva-Bharati University.

Satish Chandra (1922–2017) was a historian and Indologist who studied at the University of Allahabad (~1940–1948). He held posts as a historian at Aligarh Muslim University (~1953–1961) and at the University of Rajasthan (~1961–1970).

Satish Chandra Vidyabhusan (1870–1920) was an Indologist and Tibetologist who studied at Sanskrit College, Krishnagar Government College, and the University of Calcutta under Sarat Chandra Das. He served as Principal of Sanskrit College and held posts at The Asiatic Society.

Satkari Mookerjee (1896–1968) was a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. He served as Ashutosh Professor of Sanskrit at the University of Calcutta (~1944–1956) and became Director of Nava Nalanda Mahavihara in 1955.
Satkari Sharma Vangiya is a scholar of Indology and linguistics who studied under Ramachandra Shastri Vyakaranacharya, Ramachandra Jha, and Ramachandra Sastri.

Satoru Harada (b. 1947) is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned an MA at the University of Tokyo. He held posts at Toyo Bunko (1978), the Eastern Institute (1982), and Kokushikan University (2010–2015).

Satoru Noriyama is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied under Esho Mikogami. He held teaching posts at Osaka University of Foreign Studies (attested 1995) and Ryukoku University (attested 2003 and 2013).
Satoshi Hayashima is a scholar in Buddhist studies who studied at Ryukoku University (attested 2013) and subsequently served as a lecturer there (attested 2015–2017).

Satoshi Hiraoka (b. 1960) is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Bukkyo University and the University of Michigan. He held posts at Bukkyo University, Kyoto Bunkyo Junior College, and Kyoto Bunkyo University, where he became president in 2014.
